passage.title: What Is Misinformation?
paras: Misinformation is false or misleading information that people share without realising it is wrong. Disinformation is false information spread on purpose, to deceive.
Neither is new. Rumours have always travelled fast. What has changed is speed: a post can reach millions of people before anyone checks it.

Misinformation spreads because it often feels true. It may confirm what we already fear or believe; it is often shocking, so we want to warn others; and it usually comes from someone we trust, a friend or relative, who did not check it either.
Fear makes it worse. When people are frightened, they look for simple explanations and someone to blame, and they are less likely to stop and think.

How can you spot it? Ask: who made this, and how do they know? When was it published? Do other reliable sources report the same thing? Is the language designed to make you angry or afraid? If in doubt, do not share it.

Islam teaches the same caution: believers are told to verify news brought to them before acting on it (Qur'an 49:6). Checking before sharing is not only sensible; it is a matter of honesty and fairness to others.
